subject: pufferfish
pitch: A startled pufferfish fully puffed up into a ball. Creamy yellow skin with brown leopard spots on top fading to a white belly, short spikes all over, a tiny pouting mouth, big worried round eyes, small fluttering side fins and a stubby fan-shaped tail. A few bubbles rise from its mouth.
reasoning:

Since the pitch doesn't mention floating, I'll rest it on the ground with its lowest point touching y=0, keeping the bubbles rising naturally above the mouth as part of the model's detail rather than treating them as something separately hovering.

Sizing it realistically at roughly 0.2m diameter for the puffed body, I'm orienting it to face +Z with the tail trailing toward -Z. I'm planning the body as a lathe-generated sphere shape, using normal-based countershading to paint the belly white and the back yellow with leopard-style spots on top.

Now I'm thinking through the spikes: scattering points across the body surface and generating small spike sweeps at each one, keeping triangle count low with simple geometry (maybe 6-sided tubes, a few rings each) so 60-80 spikes stay within the overall triangle budget.

For the rig, since pufferfish have no neck, I'm planning a minimal skeleton: a root body joint near the center, plus jaw joints for mouth expression and possibly fin and tail joints, keeping the rest pose simple but structurally sound for the creature SDK's rigging requirements.

I still need to work out the mouth—separate upper and lower jaw joints so it can open and close for the pout—and the eyes, which I'll attach as children of the body joint with white sphere and dark pupil parts positioned on the upper front of the ball to give that worried expression.

For the worried look, I could angle slanted eyebrow shapes above each eye and offset pupils slightly upward and toward center. For side fins, I'm planning small fan-shaped pectoral fin joints (`finL`, `finR`) with a "fan" role, made as flat extruded slabs attached to the body surface so they can flutter. For the tail, I'm thinking a short "tail" chain with 2-3 joints topped with a fan-shaped extruded mesh—like a scalloped semicircle outline—to give it that stubby fan tail look.

I'm figuring out the fan tail's geometry: the outline sits in the plane containing the fish's length axis (Z) and vertical axis (Y), with extrusion thickness running left-right (X), so it reads as a vertical fin at the back of the ball, positioned around z = -0.09 with roughly 0.06 length, fanning outward from a point to a wide arc.

Now I'm setting up the tail as a bendable chain of joints so it can wag, defining a polyline of three points running backward from the body with names for each joint ("tail1", "tail2", "tail3") so the last one becomes the tip joint, then attaching the fan-shaped fin extrusion to that tip.

I'm also figuring out how the chain should parent to the body joint so the tail root stays attached to the body mesh, and starting to define the head/mouth placement at the front of the ball — setting up a center point and radius so I can position a small pout near the front surface, accounting for spikes adding slightly to the overall height.

Then I'm worrying about spikes placed on the bottom hemisphere potentially poking below the floor plane. I'll be safer and exclude hits with normal.y below -0.6, plus avoid the face region. Now I'm double-checking how the lathe body is constructed: the profile points trace a sphere silhouette from top to bottom, and I need to confirm this forms a closed polygon around the axis so the revolve produces a proper solid rather than an open shell.

The edge connecting the bottom pole back to the top pole lies on the axis itself, so revolving it creates zero-area degenerate triangles there — but that should render and bake fine, since both chartify and the baking logic already skip degenerate zero-area geometry. This pole-to-pole lathe profile is a standard way to build a sphere, so I'll proceed with it, defining the outline points from top pole to bottom pole using x = R sinθ, y = R cosθ.

A sphere orientation doesn't really matter since it's symmetric, so I'll keep the pufferfish body as a simple lathed sphere for the puffed-up shape, and handle features like eyes by attaching small spheres positioned using the nearest point on the body's surface.

For the eyes, I'm placing white sclera spheres with darker pupils near the front-upper region of the ball, angled slightly inward and upward to give a worried expression. Working out pupil placement...

I'll explicitly pass a `bone` option to stick so it rigs correctly to the eye joint rather than falling back to the nearest-joint default.
